sources.entry: not-th.re - Simple paste sharing platform, with client side encryption, featuring the monaco browser-based code editor. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: !3 (not-th.re) is a paste sharing platform with client-side encryption and a Monaco-based code editor, offered as a hosted service or as self-hosted API and UI deployments.
summary.what_it_does: The project provides a web UI for sharing pastes, notes and files, where content is encrypted in the browser before it is sent to the server. It includes syntax highlighting, dark mode, and file transfers. A command-line tool (@not3/cli, also available as a Docker image) can save and fetch notes, pipe logs into shared notes, and upload and download encrypted files. Bash and PowerShell scripts are also described for creating and decrypting notes and files without installing the CLI. The README lists newer features including peer-to-peer sessions, browser-local conversion/encryption/formatting tools, an HTML/JavaScript/Markdown/PHP previewer, and Excalidraw integration. The README describes "Note Bundles" as planned. Deployment options are a "micro" setup (API only, using the public UI) and a "minimal" setup with the API and UIs together, with a proxy mode on the UI.
use_cases: share code snippets with a link
pipe command output or logs to a shareable URL
preview HTML or Markdown from a paste
how_to_run: docker compose up (using the micro or minimal example YAML: ghcr.io/not-three/api:latest)
Set customServer url and password in the public UI under About -> Edit Settings (micro deployment)
notable: Client-side encryption via the Web Crypto API; the server does not see plaintext content
Monaco code editor in the browser
CLI can pipe logs or command output directly into a shared note
Shell and PowerShell scripts allow creating and decrypting notes without installing the CLI
Private instances can be linked to the public UI, with a confirmation prompt before loading data from an external server
caveats: The UI must be served over HTTPS because it depends on crypto.subtle; the README says it will not work without it
The API without SSL is described as strongly discouraged, and the example deployments do not configure SSL
Note Bundles are listed as planned, not available
